summary: Iteration 2 – Mobile-first refactor. Backend pytest 8/8 green (health/manifest now 18 images incl. cafe_patio & cafe_work_corner, both served as image/png >50KB). Frontend Playwright coverage on 390x844 + 1440x900: mobile dock, chips (7), dietary filters + autocomplete, menu Reserve prefill (Spanish Latte), Quiz flow (Spanish Latte match + reset), Chef Specials (4 cards, reserve prefill 'Interested in trying: <name>'), Reviews (Google/4.6/460+ visible, next/prev), Location (live-status 'Closed · Opens 9:30 AM' at test time, navigate href correct, tel href correct), Reservation dialog (dock opens, empty-submit shows reserve-error and no window.open, valid submit produces wa.me/919561166185?text=... containing 'Please confirm my table'), ESC closes dialog, no horiz scroll, no broken images, no console/page errors. Desktop nav shows all 6 links + Reserve; mobile dock hidden. Two minor issues found — see below.

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid is 'location-instagram-link' (from TID.locationInsta) but the review request and test spec require 'one-tap-follow' to match dock/link scheme. href value itself is correct (https://www.instagram.com/thewhitemugcafe).

integration_issues.issue: Selecting 'diet-brew' returns 14 menu items (specialty=true count in /app/frontend/src/data/menu.js). Spec expects >=15 items across Specialty Coffees + Manual Brews. Add at least 1 more specialty-flagged item OR relax spec.

action_items: Rename Location Instagram link testid from 'location-instagram-link' to 'one-tap-follow' (update /app/frontend/src/lib/testIds.js: locationInsta -> 'one-tap-follow', or change the JSX to hard-code data-testid="one-tap-follow").

Add at least one more menu item with specialty:true in /app/frontend/src/data/menu.js so diet-brew filter yields >=15 (currently 14). Candidates: any additional Manual Brew (e.g. Aeropress, Syphon) or Specialty Coffee variant.
critical_code_review_comments: TID.locationInsta constant diverges from the requested 'one-tap-*' naming used for the other two tiles (navigate/call) hard-coded inline — inconsistent testid strategy; either move all three into TID or hard-code all three.

Data drift: brief mentions 'Bestsellers … Spanish Latte, Chemex, TWM Special Frappe, Tuscan Toast, Avocado Toast, Blueberry Cheesecake — total 6' — that matches, but specialty=true only 14 vs. brief 'should be >= 15'. Consider explicit unit/constant to keep spec + data in sync.

Reservation submit relies on JS-only validation now (HTML5 required removed as noted). Good — matches spec. Ensure future refactors keep
